turns.answer:
For keeping insulin cold during a 48-hour power outage, I recommend a small portable compressor refrigerator paired with a lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) power station.

The key is maintaining 36–46°F (2–8°C) for insulin that needs refrigeration, without accidentally freezing it.

I would avoid thermoelectric mini-fridges (the inexpensive skincare or desktop coolers). They often cannot maintain a safe temperature in a hot room.

For insulin, I would also have an insulated cooler and conditioned cold packs as a backup. Keep the insulin separated from the packs to prevent freezing. The FDA notes that many insulin products can tolerate limited time at room temperature, but storage rules vary by product.
